Inside/near the band are small data points: orange/brown dots near coordinates (1,1) and (1,2) area and blue dots near (2,1) and (2,2) area, with thin dotted projection lines to the axes. A blue circle containing a white '?' sits at the lower end of the band near x1 = 7, connected by a dotted line to the x1 axis tick '7'.
Pale yellow highlighted equation banner: 'y = 0 x1 − 2 x2 + 3' with 'y' in black, '0' in blue, '−2' in red, '+3' in red; thin border around the box.

White box with thin border containing underlined heading 'Check Class of Test Vector' ('Check' underlined in blue, 'Class' in red, rest black). Below: labels X^T (blue, underlined) over row vector '(1  7  3)' with '1' in red, and W (blue, underlined) over column vector (3, 0, −2) with '3' in red and '−2' in blue. Result: '= −3' in blue, then red arrow '⇒' and 'C2' in black.
Yellow circle badge with dark outline containing slide number '35'.

recreation_brief:
1. Slide base and frame: set the slide background to light gray #F2F2F2 and draw a thin dark-red #990000 rectangle border around the entire slide edge.
2. Slide-number badge (top-right corner, circle ~2% of slide width): draw a yellow #FFFF99 circle with a thin black #000000 outline containing the black text '35'.
3. Equation banner (top-center-right, ~x 55–78%, y 10–16%): draw a pale-yellow #FFFFCC rectangle with a thin black border; inside it place the large bold equation 'y = 0 x1 − 2 x2 + 3' with '0' in blue #0000FF, '−2' and '+3' in red #FF0000, and all other characters in black.
4. Diagram panel (left half, ~x 7–52%, y 18–98%): draw a large square with a thick red #CC0000 border.
5. Inside the panel, draw the vertical 'y' axis with italic label 'y' and tick label '3'.
6. Draw the horizontal-right 'x2' axis with italic label 'x2' and tick labels '1', '2', '3'.
7. Draw the diagonal lower-left 'x1' axis with italic label 'x1' and tick labels '3' and '7'.
8. Draw a wide yellow #FFFF99 parallelogram band tilted from upper-left to lower-right across the panel and place the label 'W' at its top.
9. On the band's left edge add rotated text: blue #0000CC '-ve ( < 0 ) Class C2' above the edge and red #FF0000 '+ve ( > 0 ) Class C1' below it, plus a small blue #0000CC square marker on the boundary line.
10. Plot 2 orange/brown #CC6600 dots (one near coordinate (1,1), one near (1,2)) and 2 blue #0000CC dots (one near (2,1), one near (2,2)), each connected to the axes by thin dotted black projection lines.
11. At the lower end of the band near x1 = 7, draw a blue circle containing a white '?' and join it to the x1-axis tick '7' with a dotted line.
12. Calculation panel (right-center, ~x 55–88%, y 38–68%): draw a white #FFFFFF rectangle with a thin black border.
13. Inside the calculation panel, place the underlined heading 'Check Class of Test Vector' with 'Check' in blue #0000FF, 'Class' in red #FF0000, and 'of Test Vector' in black.
14. Below the heading, reproduce the equation 'y = (1  7  3) · (3, 0, −2)^T = −3 ⇒ C2': place the label 'X^T' (blue #0000FF, underlined) above the row vector '(1  7  3)' with '1' in red and the other entries in black; place the label 'W' (blue #0000FF, underlined) above the vertical column vector '(3, 0, −2)' with '3' in red, '0' in black, and '−2' in blue; then place '= −3' in blue #0000FF, a red #FF0000 '⇒' arrow, and 'C2' in black.
